<details class="topic-card" open>
<summary>Syntax / typing</summary>
<div class="topic-card-body">

Work through one bug at a time. In each code block: run it, fix it, and re-run.

## 1) Typos in names

```{webr}
# Challenge: fix the object-name typo
data <- 10
Data + 5
```

<details>
<summary>Show solution</summary>

```{webr}
data <- 10
data + 5
```

</details>

<hr>

## 2) `=` vs `==` in conditions

```{webr}
# Challenge: this should test equality, not assign
x <- 3
if (x = 3) {
  "x is three"
}
```

<details>
<summary>Show solution</summary>

```{webr}
x <- 3
if (x == 3) {
  "x is three"
}
```

</details>

<hr>

## 3) Unbalanced parentheses or quotes

```r
# Challenge (run in your R console):
cat("Dose is", 75
```

If your console prompt changes from `>` to `+`, R is waiting for the missing closing character.

<details>
<summary>Show solution</summary>

```r
cat("Dose is", 75)
```

</details>

<hr>

## 4) Missing commas in function arguments

```{webr}
# Challenge: add the missing comma
paste("Batch" "A")
```

<details>
<summary>Show solution</summary>

```{webr}
paste("Batch", "A")
```

</details>

<hr>

## 5) Spacing bug: `x < -3` vs `x <- 3`

```{webr}
# Challenge: assign 3 to x (do not compare)
x < -3
x
```

<details>
<summary>Show solution</summary>

```{webr}
x <- 3
x
```

</details>

</div>
</details>

<details class="topic-card">
<summary>Common R pitfalls</summary>
<div class="topic-card-body">

### 1) `[ ]` vs `[[ ]]` on lists

```{webr}
# Challenge: make this return 80 (not an error)
my_list <- list(batch = "A", dose_mg = 75)
dose <- my_list["dose_mg"]
dose + 5
```

<details>
<summary>Show solution</summary>

```{webr}
my_list <- list(batch = "A", dose_mg = 75)
dose <- my_list[["dose_mg"]]
dose + 5
```

</details>

### 2) `NA` handling

```{webr}
# Challenge: compute the mean and find missing values correctly
x <- c(10, 12, NA, 9)
mean(x)
x == NA
```

<details>
<summary>Show solution</summary>

```{webr}
x <- c(10, 12, NA, 9)
mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
is.na(x)
```

</details>

### 3) Floating-point comparisons

```{webr}
# Challenge: this prints FALSE. Use a safer check.
0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3
```

<details>
<summary>Show solution</summary>

```{webr}
all.equal(0.1 + 0.2, 0.3)
abs((0.1 + 0.2) - 0.3) < 1e-12
```

</details>

### 4) Not assigning results

```{webr}
# Challenge: sort x and keep the sorted result in x
x <- c(3, 1, 2)
sort(x)
x
```

<details>
<summary>Show solution</summary>

```{webr}
x <- c(3, 1, 2)
x <- sort(x)
x
```

</details>

### 5) `library()` vs `install.packages()`

```r
# Challenge:
# 1) Install once on your computer
# 2) Load every new R session

install.packages("tidyverse")  # run once (not every script run)
library(tidyverse)              # run each session
```

After restarting R, run `library(tidyverse)` again before using tidyverse functions.

### 6) Reading error messages

```{webr}
# Challenge: find and fix the typo based on the first error line
library(tidyverse)

df <- tibble(weight_mg = c(100, 101, 99))
df %>%
  mutate(weight_g = wieght_mg / 1000)
```

<details>
<summary>Show solution</summary>

```{webr}
library(tidyverse)

df <- tibble(weight_mg = c(100, 101, 99))
df %>%
  mutate(weight_g = weight_mg / 1000)
```

</details>

Tip: read errors top to bottom. Start with the first line that names the missing object, function, or argument.

</div>
</details>

<details class="topic-card">
<summary>Object and data errors</summary>
<div class="topic-card-body">

Common messages include:

- `object 'name' not found`
- `subscript out of bounds`
- `NAs introduced by coercion`

These usually mean one of three things: the object was never created, a column name is wrong, or a conversion (for example text to numeric) failed.

```{webr}
library(tidyverse)

df <- tibble(
  id = 1:3,
  conc_text = c("4.1", "5.0", "bad")
)

df %>%
  mutate(conc_num = as.numeric(conc_text))
```

Tip: use `names(df)`, `glimpse(df)`, and `head(df)` before complex transformations.

</div>
</details>

<details class="topic-card">
<summary>Function, package, and argument errors</summary>
<div class="topic-card-body">

If R says it "could not find function", check that the package is installed and loaded.

```r
install.packages("tidyverse")  # once per computer
library(tidyverse)              # every new session
```

If a function call fails:

- Read the first error line first
- Verify argument names in `?function_name`
- Check data types expected by the function

Example: [`filter()`](../functions/filter.qmd) expects logical conditions, while [`mutate()`](../functions/mutate.qmd) expects name-expression pairs.

</div>
</details>

<details class="topic-card">
<summary>A simple debugging workflow</summary>
<div class="topic-card-body">

Use this sequence when code fails:

1. Re-run only the failing line or chunk.
2. Print intermediate objects (`head()`, `glimpse()`, `summary()`).
3. Simplify to a minimal reproducible example.
4. Check types (`class()`, `typeof()`, `is.na()`).
5. Add one step back at a time until the error returns.

For pipelines, break them into named steps temporarily:

```{webr}
library(tidyverse)

step1 <- read_csv("data/capsules.csv")
step2 <- step1 %>% filter(batch == "A")
step3 <- step2 %>% mutate(adj_pct = pct_label - 100)

glimpse(step3)
```

This helps isolate where the problem starts.

</div>
</details>
